Title: Withdrawal of service
Content: Item revenue upon service withdrawal When you withdraw from the service, posting and selling of all items will be discontinued. If items previously sold by a seller who withdrew from the service are used as Design Source for new items and those new items are sold, the revenue will not be paid to the seller who withdrew from the service. When a seller withdraws from the service, the final revenue will be settled in the following month.
ContentDescription: This web page clarifies the revenue policies regarding item sales and withdrawals from the service, outlining the impact on sellers' earnings and the timeline for final revenue settlement.

Title: Blocking items
Content: When Items are Blocked Items, either in whole or in part, may be blocked if they infringe on someone else's copyright. Items that are explicit or violent may be blocked. Items containing messages that are potentially controversial in areas such as politics or religion may be blocked. Items that cause discomfort to other users or receive continuous reports may be blocked. In cases where items are deemed incompatible with the policies of CONNECT, administrators may block them. Revenue when Paid Items are Blocked If a paid item is blocked, sales will be discontinued. Revenue from already sold items will be paid to the seller. If the reason for blocking the item is related to copyright, ownership of revenue from already sold items may be determined through legal procedures or discussions with the original creator. If a blocked item is used as a Design Source, generating revenue, the seller will not receive any revenue.
ContentDescription: This web page outlines the policies and procedures for blocking items that infringe on copyright, violate community standards, or cause user discomfort, along with guidelines for revenue implications when paid items are blocked.

Title: Payout Schedule
Content: Payout in the following month Revenue from items sold between the 1st and last day of each month will be settled in the following month. Payout dates fall between the 15th and 30th of the following month, subject to variation due to holidays or maintenance. Wire Transfer Schedule Revenue from December to May will be paid out in June. Revenue from June to November will be paid in December. If an account has an issue on the payout day, it will be postponed to the next scheduled payout day. Refund Policy Refunds due to technical issues or payment cancellations will be deducted from the final revenue before the settlement date.
ContentDescription: This webpage outlines the payout schedule, refund policy, and wire transfer timelines for revenue generated from sales, ensuring clarity on when and how payments are processed.

Title: Payout conditions
Content: To process settlement, ensure the following conditions are met: Seller's Information Verification Once seller's information is verified, the payout will be processed. Revenue accumulates before verification the payout is available once seller info is verified. When seller information is changed after initial verification, payout will be delayed for re-verification. Payout Available over USD $50 Access payout when total revenue, after fee deduction, exceeds USD $50. If revenue is under USD $50, expected payout accumulates. The payout is based on the sales revenue of $50 USD (taxes are not included). If you have US-resident buyers, their tax is deducted from the final payout. Note that the actual payout may vary after tax deductions. Payout Delayed Payout delays occur in the presence of copyright issues until resolution. Majority of buyer refund requests or submitted reports result in payout delay until it is solved. Payout will be temporarily disabled in cases of suspicious payments or payment system issues.
ContentDescription: This web page outlines the conditions and procedures for processing seller payouts, including verification requirements, payout thresholds, and potential delays due to verification issues or disputes.

Title: Design Source Policy
Content: Create items using paid items (garments/trims/fabrics) You may sell created items by using paid items(garments/ trims/ fabrics). Garments can be purchased, modified, and sold as a second creation on CONNECT. However, trims and fabrics cannot be modified and re-sell. Trims can be only included in garments. Settlement when using paid items When created garments consist of paid items as a Design Source, the price of paid items will be added to your set price. When garments consisting of paid items are sold, the revenue of the Design Source will be distributed to the original creator. Revenue when your items are sold as Design Source When your items are sold and used as Design Source for other items, your items will be settled as your revenue. Examples Seller D created garments by purchasing Seller A's garment($10), Seller B's trim($2), Seller C's fabric($5). When Seller D sets the price of the garment, the total price will be automatically set as the sum of items A, B, and C, which is $17. When Seller D sets the margin as $20, the total price will be $37. When items are sold at $37, Seller D's revenue will be $20, Seller A's will be $10, Seller B's $2, Seller C's $5.
ContentDescription: This web page outlines the process for creating and selling custom garments using purchased items, detailing how revenue is generated and distributed among creators.

Title: Deduction amount & Payout amount
Content: The calculation of the seller's earnings is as follows. Total item sales amount (-) Design Source usage fee (-) Website deduction commission (-) Withholding tax Total item sales amount Total amount of items sold from the first to the last day of the month Includes items sold through Design Source when other sellers' items are sold (When someone resells my item as a component in a garment file, the price of my item is included in my sales revenue) (-) Design Source usage fee If paid items are used, the revenue is shared with the seller who created those items. (When a paid garment, fabric, or trims are purchased to create a paid garment, and the garment is sold, the price of the included paid items is categorized as the sales revenue of the seller of those items) (-) Website Commission Deduction 70% of the total sales amount is allocated as the seller's revenue, while 30% is deducted as a service fee. (-) Withholding tax For orders where the buyer is American, a withholding tax may be additionally applied. The withholding tax rate is calculated based on the agreed upon rate between the United States and the seller's country. [Example] Without using Design Source, a $100 item was created and sold, with the buyer not being from the United States, Total Sales Amount: $100 (-) Website Commission: $30 = Total Payment: $70 Using $10 fabric, a $100 item was created and sold, with the buyer not being from the United States, Total Sales Amount: $100 (-) Cost of Design Source Fabric: $10 (-) Website Commission: $27(30%) = Total Payment: $63 A Polish individual created a $100 item without using Design Source and sold it to a buyer from the United States, Total Sales Amount: $100 (-) Website Commission(30%): $30 = User's Earnings: $70 (-) Withholding Tax (5% between Poland and the United States): $3.5 = Total Payment: $66.5 A Korean individual created a $100 item using $30 buttons and sold it to a buyer from the United States, Total Sales Amount: $100 (-) Cost of Design Source Buttons: $30 (-) Website Commission(30%): $21 = User's Earnings: $49 (-) Withholding Tax (10% between South Korea and the United States): $4.9 = Total Payment: $44.1
ContentDescription: This web page outlines the detailed calculation of seller earnings, factoring in total sales, design source fees, website commission, and any applicable withholding taxes.

Title: Seller Information Guide
Content: Find Seller Information Here 1) Select the profile image at the top right of the CONNECT page. 2) Select the Sales menu. 3) Select the INFO tab on the Sales page. Enter Seller Info 1) Press the CREATE button at the very bottom of the INFO page to start editing. 2) After accurately entering information for each item, select the seller type in the TAX INFORMATION section. Non US seller (Individual): For individuals who are not corporations, including those who are not American or Americans who do not reside in the USA. Non US seller (Entities): Corporations from countries other than the USA, including corporations established abroad by Americans. US Seller: Americans who pay taxes in the USA, or American corporations. 3) Download the tax file according to the selected Type by clicking on the Download Link. 4) After completing the Tax document, press 'Choose File' to attach the file you have prepared. (Please refer to the manual for how to complete the tax document). 5) Upon completing all required fields, finalize your submission by clicking the SUBMIT button. Seller Info Submission Status Pending Once the Seller Info submission is complete, a status value of PENDING will appear at the top. The information must be reviewed and approved by an administrator for the Seller Info registration to be finally completed. The review process can take from 1 to a maximum of 10 business days. During the Pending status, the information can be edited or updated. Rejected This status indicates that the Seller Info has not been finally approved and has been rejected. By clicking the message icon to the right of the REJECTED text, you can view the reasons for the rejection. You can modify the Seller Info and resubmit it by pressing the SUBMIT button again. Confirmed Your Seller Info registration has been finally approved. If your earnings meet the CONNECT payment conditions, you can start receiving payments from the next scheduled payment date. If you modify the information in the Confirmed status, it will revert to Pending, and the information will be reviewed again. Earnings received during the review and approval process will be paid based on the previous information. (If you need to modify your information, it should be done before the 10th of each month.)
ContentDescription: This webpage provides a step-by-step guide for sellers to submit and manage their seller information, including tax documentation and status updates throughout the review process.

Title: Material Tab
Content: EveryWear Tutorial 1) UV Packing Objective Customize the resolution and spacing of UV and automatically reposition the UV shell accordingly. Details You can select the resolution of the UV image. Adjust the spacing of UV that are automatically placed when packing UVs. Go to the UV packing settings window. The EveryWear window will close for a moment. 1-1) UV Packing_Option Objective Set and apply UV Packing-related options. Details Option to set the UV accuracy from 1 to 5. Values closer to 5 will pack the UVs more accurately to their original form but may increase the amount of calculation and packing time. Fix Scale Ratio : When enabled, it adjusts the size of the entire UV shell while maintaining the spacing ratio between UV shells. Rotation : When enabled, it allows for the rotation of the UV shell. Advanced Placement : When enabled, it uses an advanced calculation method to achieve optimal placement with minimal empty space, but the process may take longer as the number of patterns increases. Fill the U:0, V:0 tiles with the selected UV Shell. Pack the selected UV Shell directly by specifying the target tile. Initialize all user-specified option values. Pack UVs according to the specified option values. Close the UV packing window and return to the EveryWear window. 2) Texture Baking Objective Create maps that express the details of the High Poly model in the optimized model. (Normal &amp A.O.) Details Create a Normal Map and Ambient Occlusion (A.O) Map. Adjust the intensity of the Baked Normal Map. The number of rays of light sampled per pixel. Increase this value for higher-quality, but please keep in mind that it will also increase calculation time. Activate this option to preview the baked map in the 3D viewport. This allows you to see the changes in real-time. Delete Baked Map 3) Material List Objective Copy an existing material or create a new material, and apply it to the selected pattern as desired. Details Add a new Material item. Copy a Material. Assign the selected Material to the selected Object. Delete the selected Material. You cannot delete the material that is already assigned to the Object.
ContentDescription: This web page provides a comprehensive tutorial on UV packing, texture baking, and material management in EveryWear, enabling users to optimize their 3D models with precision and efficiency.

Title: Cautionary Notes for Upload
Content: EveryWear Tutorial 1) Cautionary Notes for Upload Objective If the conditions for Upload are not valid, the following window will be displayed. Details An avatar with joints must be in the 3D window. All patterns must be rigged. All UVs must be packed. (An UV must be placed within a tile.) Normal Map must be baked.
ContentDescription: This webpage provides essential guidelines and cautionary notes for successfully uploading 3D models in the EveryWear platform.

Title: Upload to CONNECT
Content: EveryWear Tutorial 1) Upload to CONNECT Objective You can upload your created items to CONNECT. Details Upload your created items to CONNECT. Upon selection, the FBX Options window will appear. The EveryWear window will close. Select the object(s) to upload. At least one item must be selected. Choose the textures to export. Select the texture options. Embed Media : The textures will be sent as a zip file along with the project. Graphic Library : Choose the appropriate format for the platform, either OpenGL or DirectX. Initialize all user-specified option values. Upload to CONNECT according to the specified option values. Close the FBX options window and navigate to the EveryWear window. To save the project, close the EveryWear window and save it as a ZPRJ file. [Main menu] - [File] - [Save as] - [Project]
ContentDescription: This webpage provides a step-by-step tutorial on how to upload your created items to CONNECT using the EveryWear platform.

Title: Preparing and Starting EveryWear
Content: EveryWear Tutorial 1. What to prepare? To use EveryWear, you must utilize the Auto Fitting function to dress the outfit on the avatar of the platform you intend to export it to. Auto Fitting Conditions The Auto Fitting function can only be utilized when avatars are wearing a fitting suit. A fitting suit can be generated either automatically or manually (only in Marvelous Designer)when loading an avatar. If you attempt to use the fitting function with an avatar that doesn't have a fitting suit, the following warning message will appear, and the fitting function will not be applied. To utilize EveryWear, the avatar must have joints and be rigged. 2. Started with EveryWear Click on the CONNECT - EveryWear button in the top menu of the program. To use EveryWear, make sure you meet the following two conditions: Complete the sign-in process in the Library &gt&gt Connect tab Ensure you have completed the EveryWear Creator registration. / EveryWear Creator registration
ContentDescription: This webpage provides essential guidelines for preparing and utilizing the EveryWear platform, ensuring users understand the requirements for successfully applying the Auto Fitting function to their avatars.

Title: What is EveryWear?
Content: EveryWear is a feature package that optimizes garments made in CLO and Marvelous Designer for digital spaces like gaming, metaverse, and entertainment. Subscribers of CLO and Marvelous Designer can access these features for free during the beta phase. For additional information, please visit our website. EveryWear will significantly reduce your time and costs by automating repetitive tasks. Here is a list of features that will streamline the process of converting your 3D garment to the digital space. #1. Fitting Auto Fitting automatically adjusts 2D patterns and 3D garment to fit the size/body of the avatar. It allows creators to easily modify clothing designed for different avatar sizes/body to fit the other avatars in different sizes. #2. Rigging Rigging involves attaching 3D garment to a character and defining how it moves and behaves in real-time application like video games. It allows creators to significantly reduce the time required for rigging. #3. Texture Baking Texture baking is to capture and transfer information from high-resolution 3D garment to 2D texture maps. It allows creators to improve the efficiency and and increase the realism of 3D garments. #4. Level of Detail Level of Detail (LoD) involves creating different versions of a 3D character and dynamically selecting which one to render based on the viewer's distance. Creators don't need to worry about LoD, as it automatically generates the other levels based on the creator's original design. EveryWear Tutorial
ContentDescription: Discover EveryWear, a powerful feature package that streamlines the optimization of CLO and Marvelous Designer garments for digital environments, offering automated solutions to enhance efficiency and reduce costs during its free beta phase.
